'''Greta Albrecht Fryxell''' (November 21, 1926 – September 24, 2017) was a marine scientist known for her work on the biology and taxonomy of [[diatom]]s. In 1996, she was elected a fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].

== Education and career ==
Fryxell graduated summa cum laude from [[Augustana College (Illinois)|Augustana College]] in 1948 and then taught in junior high schools in Iowa. She was one of the first women admitted to [[Texas A&M University]] where she first earned a masters in education in 1969.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last=Medlin|first=Linda K.|date=2018-01-02|title=Obituary – Greta A. Fryxell|url=https://doi.org/10.1080/0269249X.2017.1419988|journal=Diatom Research|volume=33|issue=1|pages=123–133|doi=10.1080/0269249X.2017.1419988|bibcode=2018DiaRe..33..123M |s2cid=90844546|issn=0269-249X}}</ref> In 1975, she earned her Ph.D. from Texas A&M University working on the taxonomy of select [[diatom]]s.<ref>{{Cite thesis|title=Morphology, taxonomy, and distribution of selected diatom species of Thalassiosira Cleve in the Gulf of Mexico and Antarctic waters|date=1975|language=English|first=Greta A|last=Fryxell|oclc = 42675078}}</ref> Fryxell worked at Texas A&M University and the [[University of Texas at Austin]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite news|date=23 August 1996|title=NEWS FROM The University of Texas at Austin MARINE SCIENCE INSTITUTE|volume=5|work=The Lazarette Gazette|issue=12|url=https://repositories.lib.utexas.edu/bitstream/handle/2152/41414/txu-oclc-317299931-05-12.txt?sequence=2&isAllowed=y|access-date=October 31, 2021}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite web|date=September 1, 2008|title=Greta Fryxell Honored|url=https://www.psaalgae.org/news/2014/11/14/greta-fryxell-honored|access-date=2021-10-30|website=Phycological Society of America|language=en-US}}</ref>

== Research ==
Fryxell is known for her research on phytoplankton, especially diatoms, where she combined investigations of laboratory cultures with samples collected from a variety of locations including the North Atlantic,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Fryxell|first1=G.A.|last2=Gould|first2=R.W.|last3=Watkins|first3=T.P.|date=1984|title=Gelatinous colonies of the diatom Thalassiosira in Gulf Stream Warm Core Rings including T. fragilis, sp. nov.|url=http://www.tandfonline.com/doi/abs/10.1080/00071618400650151|journal=British Phycological Journal|language=en|volume=19|issue=2|pages=141–156|doi=10.1080/00071618400650151|issn=0007-1617|url-access=subscription}}</ref> [[Gulf of Mexico]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Dortch|first1=Q|last2=Robichaux|first2=R|last3=Pool|first3=S|last4=Milsted|first4=D|last5=Mire|first5=G|last6=Rabalais|first6=NN|author-link6=Nancy Rabalais|last7=Soniat|first7=TM|last8=Fryxell|first8=GA|last9=Turner|first9=RE|last10=Parsons|first10=Ml|date=1997|title=Abundance and vertical flux of Pseudo-nitzschia in the northern Gulf of Mexico|url=http://www.int-res.com/abstracts/meps/v146/p249-264/|journal=Marine Ecology Progress Series|language=en|volume=146|pages=249–264|doi=10.3354/meps146249|bibcode=1997MEPS..146..249D|issn=0171-8630|doi-access=free}}</ref> and Antarctica.<ref name=":0" /> She established a framework for phytoplankton taxonomy and, on her 70th birthday, the ''Fryxelliella'' genus of diatoms was named after her to acknowledge her work on diatom taxonomy and biology.<ref name="doi.org">{{Cite journal|last1=Prasad|first1=A. K. S. K.|last2=Riddle|first2=K. A.|last3=Livingston|first3=R. J.|date=1997-07-01|title=Fine structure, taxonomy, and systematics of the centric diatom Fryxelliella gen. nov. (Eupodiscaceae, Bacillariophyta) having a new valve structure, the circumferential marginal tube, with descriptions of F. floridana sp. nov. and F. inconspicua (Rattray) comb. nov.|url=https://doi.org/10.2216/i0031-8884-36-4-305.1|journal=Phycologia|volume=36|issue=4|pages=305–323|doi=10.2216/i0031-8884-36-4-305.1|bibcode=1997Phyco..36..305P |issn=0031-8884|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite magazine|date=Spring 2002|title=Fantastic Voyage|url=https://cdn.txamfoundation.com/Spirit/Spirit%20archives%20rotator%20photos/Spirit%20archive%20PDFs/2002_spring_spirit.pdf|publisher=Texas A&M Foundation|pages=6–7|access-date=October 30, 2021}}</ref>

In 1970, Fryxell worked with [[Grethe Rytter Hasle]] to describe a means to prepare diatom samples for microscopy.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Hasle|first1=Grethe R.|last2=Fryxell|first2=Greta A.|date=1970|title=Diatoms: Cleaning and Mounting for Light and Electron Microscopy|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/3224555|journal=Transactions of the American Microscopical Society|volume=89|issue=4|pages=469|doi=10.2307/3224555|jstor=3224555|url-access=subscription}}</ref> They would go on to jointly publish many species descriptions <ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Fryxell|first1=Greta A.|last2=Hasle|first2=Grethe R.|title=Thalassiosira Eccentrica(Ehrenb.) Cleve, T. Symmetricasp. Nov., and Some Related Centric Diatoms1|date=1972|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/j.1529-8817.1972.tb04044.x|journal=Journal of Phycology|language=en|volume=8|issue=4|pages=297–317|doi=10.1111/j.1529-8817.1972.tb04044.x|bibcode=1972JPcgy...8..297F |s2cid=86683111|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Fryxell|first1=G. == Awards and honors ==
In 1997, the Genus ''Fryxelliella'' was named in honor of Fryxell's work on diatoms.<ref name="doi.org"/><ref>{{cite journal|last1=Aké-Castillo|first1=José Antolín|last2=DEL CASTILLO|first2=MARÍA ESTHER MEAVE|last3=ZAMUDIO-RESENDIZ|first3=MARÍA EUGENIA|date=7 February 2014|title=Nomenclatural priority of the diatom name Fryxelliella sepulvedana over Fryxelliella pacifica (Triceratiaceae, Bacillariophyta)|journal=Phytotaxa|volume=159|issue=1|pages=11|doi=10.11646/phytotaxa.159.1.2|bibcode=2014Phytx.159...11A |s2cid=55304368 |issn=1179-3163|doi-access=free}}</ref> Other phytoplankton named after Fryxell include ''Actinocyclus fryxelliae'' Barron,<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Baldauf|first1=J. G.|last2=Barron|first2=J. A.|year=1991|title=Diatom biostratigraphy: Kerguelen Plateau and Prydz Bay regions of the Southern Ocean|journal=Proceedings of the Ocean Drilling Program, Scientific Results|volume=119|pages=547–598}}</ref> P''oloniasira fryxelliana'' I. Kaczmarska & J.M. Ehrman,<ref>{{cite journal|title=Poloniasira fryxelliana Kaczmarska and Ehrman, a new thalassiosiroid diatom (Bacillariophyta) from the Lower Ologocene diatomites in Polish Flysch Carpathians, southern Poland|journal=Beihefte zur Nova Hedwigia|volume=133|pages=217–230}}</ref> and ''Thalassiosira fryxelliae.''<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Sunesen|first1=Inés|last2=Sar|first2=Eugenia A.|date=2004-07-12|title=Thalassiosira fryxelliae nov. spec. (Bacillariophyceae) from Argentinian coastal waters|journal=Botanica Marina|url=https://www.degruyter.com/document/doi/10.1515/BOT.2004.025/html|language=en|volume=47|issue=3|pages=238–247|doi=10.1515/BOT.2004.025|bibcode=2004BoMar..47...25S |s2cid=86200784|url-access=subscription}}</ref> In 1988, she received the Provasoli Award<ref>{{Cite web|title=Provasoli Award|url=https://www.psaalgae.org/provasoli-award|access-date=2021-10-30|website=Phycological Society of America|language=en-US}}</ref> of the [[Phycological Society of America]] for a paper she co-authored with A. Michelle Wood and [[Russell Lande]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Wood|first1=A. Michelle|last2=Lande|first2=Russell|last3=Fryxell|first3=Greta A.|date=1987|title=Quantitative Genetic Analysis of Morphological Variation in an Antarctic Diatom Grown at Two Light Intensities1|url=https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1111/j.1529-8817.1987.tb04425.x|journal=Journal of Phycology|language=en|volume=23|issue=2|pages=42–54|doi=10.1111/j.1529-8817.1987.tb04425.x|s2cid=85666613|issn=1529-8817|url-access=subscription}}</ref> In 1996, she received the Phycological Society of America's Award of Excellence.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Award of Excellence|url=https://www.psaalgae.org/award-of-excellence|access-date=2021-10-30|website=Phycological Society of America|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name=":1" /> She also received a Distinguished Achievement Award in Research from Texas A&M's Former Students' Association (1991)<ref>{{Cite web|date=1991|title=Greta Fryxell '69|url=https://www.aggienetwork.com/tribute/index/276-18/|access-date=2021-10-30|website=www.aggienetwork.com}}</ref> and was elected a fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science in 1996.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Historic Fellows {{!}} American Association for the Advancement of Science|url=https://www.aaas.org/fellows/historic|access-date=2021-10-30|website=www.aaas.org|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=University of Texas Marine Science Institute|date=1996-11-08|title=Greta Fryxell named AAAS Fellow|url=https://repositories.lib.utexas.edu/handle/2152/41417|journal=Lazarette Gazette|language=en|volume=5|issue=15|pages=8|doi=10.15781/T2125QB42 }}</ref> In 2008, there was a [[festschrift]] in her honor.<ref>{{Cite book|title=Phytoplankton evolution, taxonomy and ecology|date=2008|publisher=J. == Personal life ==
She married the botanist [[Paul Fryxell]] in 1947.<ref name=":0" /> Three of her children contributed to the 2008 festschrift in her honor: Karl J Fryxell, Joan E. Fryxell, and Glen E. Fryxell.<ref name=":2" />
